questions.question: The RN plans discharge teaching, but the client reports severe pain and cannot focus. What should the RN do first?
choices: Give all instructions quickly before the client becomes more tired
Address and reassess the pain according to the care plan, then teach when the client can participate
Ask the client to sign that teaching was offered
Leave written material and record the teaching as complete
questions.explanation: Severe pain interferes with attention and learning readiness. The RN addresses the immediate need, reassesses the client, and chooses a time and method that allow meaningful participation.

questions.question: A client with limited English proficiency needs teaching about a new high-risk medication. Which plan is best?
choices: Ask the client’s young child to interpret the instructions
Use an online translation chosen by another patient
Arrange a qualified health care interpreter, speak directly to the client, and verify understanding
Teach only the English-speaking family member even though the client can make decisions
questions.explanation: A qualified interpreter supports accurate, impartial communication while preserving the client’s confidentiality and decision-making authority. The RN speaks to and teaches the capable client directly.

questions.question: Which statement is the best example of teach-back?
choices: I want to be sure I explained this clearly. Please tell me how you will take this medicine at home
Do you understand everything I just told you?
Repeat my exact words so I can grade your memory
You read well, so I know you will follow the instructions
questions.explanation: Effective teach-back places responsibility on the clinician’s explanation and asks the learner to describe the plan in their own words. A yes-or-no question does not demonstrate usable understanding.

questions.question: A client gives an incorrect teach-back of wound-care instructions. What should the RN do next?
choices: Document noncompliance and end the session
Repeat the same instructions more loudly
Ask a family member to perform all care without the client’s permission
Re-explain the missed step in a different way and ask the client to teach it back again
questions.explanation: An incorrect teach-back signals that communication or the plan needs adjustment. The RN clarifies without shame, changes the teaching approach, checks for barriers, and reassesses understanding.

questions.question: Which method best evaluates whether a client can safely use a newly prescribed inhaler?
choices: Ask whether the written instructions were read
Have the client perform a complete return demonstration while the RN observes
Ask whether a relative has used an inhaler
Record teaching complete after showing a video
questions.explanation: A psychomotor skill is best evaluated through return demonstration. Observing the complete sequence allows the RN to identify errors, give respectful correction, and confirm safe performance.

questions.question: Which learning outcome is written in measurable, learner-centered terms?
choices: The RN will review fall prevention
The client will receive a brochure
Before discharge, the client will demonstrate use of the walker and state when to request assistance
Teaching will occur sometime today
questions.explanation: The outcome identifies what the client will demonstrate and explain and sets a time for evaluation. The other choices describe nursing activity or material delivery rather than learner performance.

questions.question: Which finding most clearly shows that written discharge material needs adaptation?
choices: The client asks an appropriate follow-up question
The client prefers to review information in the morning
The client’s support person brings a notebook
The client cannot read the small print even while wearing prescribed glasses
questions.explanation: Material that the client cannot see is not accessible. The RN provides a usable format and combines it with clear spoken teaching and verification rather than treating document delivery as education.

questions.question: After teaching a client to measure a new liquid medication, which finding best demonstrates learning?
choices: The client nods while the RN speaks
The client signs the discharge form
The client selects the supplied oral syringe, measures the prescribed volume correctly, and explains the schedule
The family says the medication is probably similar to one used before
questions.explanation: Correct return demonstration plus explanation provides observable evidence that the client can use the device and follow the schedule. Nodding, signing, or family assumptions do not confirm learning.

questions.question: An alert client wants a support person included in teaching. What should the RN do?
choices: Include the support person with the client’s permission while continuing to direct education and decisions to the capable client
Teach only the support person because it saves time
Exclude all support people from education
Allow the support person to change the plan without asking the client
questions.explanation: Chosen support persons can reinforce learning when the client agrees, but they do not replace the capable client’s participation or authority. The RN maintains privacy and centers the client.

questions.question: Which documentation best records the outcome of patient education?
choices: Teaching done
Client verbalized understanding
Brochure left at bedside
Client used teach-back to state the dose and timing correctly but omitted the warning sign; RN re-taught the warning sign and client then identified when to call
questions.explanation: Specific documentation records the evaluation method, demonstrated learning, remaining gap, corrective teaching, and reassessment. General phrases do not show what the learner can explain or do.
